sources.title: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine, Reproducibility and Replicability in Science (2019), Chapter 3: Understanding Reproducibility and Replicability
sources.locator: Chapter 3 full-text passages, printed pp. 39–54: terminology discussion and Conclusion 3-1, pp. 39–46; precision and methods discussion, pp. 46–52; Box 3-2, Finding 3-1, and transparency discussion, pp. 53–54.

contents.name: Chapter 3 introduction: reproducibility and replicability terminology varies across disciplines
Conclusion 3-1: computational reproducibility uses the same inputs and analysis conditions; replicability uses new study data for the same question
Generalizability paragraph following Conclusion 3-1: findings in different contexts or populations
Precision-of-measurement discussion and Box 3-1 metrology terminology
contents.reason: Measurement precision and metrological repeatability are not developed here; this pair uses only the report's uncertainty caveat when interpreting replication consistency.

contents.name: Methods variation discussion, printed pp. 51–52: small procedural differences can affect study results
Box 3-2: data collection, cleaning, grouping, and curation decisions, including same-raw-data team analyses
Rigor and transparency discussion: report measurements, preparation, planned and unplanned analyses, and uncertainty
Finding 3-1: computational reproduction can be possible while a sound study still fails to replicate

sources.title: Greg Wilson, Jennifer Bryan, Karen Cranston, Justin Kitzes, Lex Nederbragt, and Tracy K. Teal, Good enough practices in scientific computing, PLoS Computational Biology 13(6):e1005510 (2017)
sources.locator: Full text: Overview and Introduction; Data management; Software; Project organization; Keeping track of changes; Inadvertent sharing; and Manuscripts.

contents.name: Overview and Introduction: organized data, documented computing steps, and project structure support reproducible workflows
Data management: preserve raw data, document processing steps, and retain intermediate data products
Data metadata and project organization: describe records, metadata, and data-processing products clearly
Software: make program use and computational dependencies explicit
Keeping track of changes: document changes to project components over time
Inadvertent sharing: legal restrictions may prohibit public release of sensitive data
Manuscript collaboration workflows and version control details
contents.reason: This pair records reporting content and computational conditions; it does not prescribe manuscript collaboration software or a version-control workflow.
